model_frontier_decision.reason: fixed mixed frontier: semantic leader, posterior anchors, and relevant components

evidence: Revert of SelectionDAG legalization work, so it can perturb backend DAG shapes
But it only undoes CTTZ_ELTS support and does not match the X86 assertion mechanism
features: SelectionDAG, intrinsic lowering, meta:core-llvm, meta:revert, path:llvm/include/llvm/CodeGen, path:llvm/lib/CodeGen/SelectionDAG
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This revert removes the previously added SelectionDAG legalization and expansion support for ISD::CTTZ_ELTS and ISD::CTTZ_ELTS_ZERO_POISON, undoing the new split/promotion handling and deleting the generic TargetLowering::expandCttzElts implementation and its declaration. It also restores SelectionDAGBuilder to directly emit the intrinsic node rather than expanding it through the new helper.
Changed symbols: DAGTypeLegalizer::SplitVectorOperand; DAGTypeLegalizer::PromoteIntegerOperand; SelectionDAGBuilder::visitIntrinsicCall; TargetLowering::expandCttzElts; VectorLegalizer::LegalizeOp; VectorLegalizer::Expand
Behavioral change: Removes legalization hooks for CTTZ_ELTS/CTTZ_ELTS_ZERO_POISON in vector splitting and integer promotion.; Removes the generic expansion helper that computed trailing-zero element counts via vector reduction.; Restores direct intrinsic node emission in SelectionDAGBuilder instead of custom expansion logic.; Eliminates the new legalization/expansion path for these nodes, reverting behavior to the prior state.
Assertion or trace link: low bits constraint must survive width adjustment; peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc; combineBTToBitOpFlag; X86ISelLowering.cpp
Reproducer link: Clang crashes at -O1; X86 DAG instruction selection assertion; backend crash during SelectionDAG combine
Pass or subsystem link: SelectionDAG; LegalizeVectorTypes; LegalizeIntegerTypes; LegalizeVectorOps; SelectionDAGBuilder
Causal explanation: This revert only undoes the CTTZ_ELTS legalization work and does not modify the X86-specific combine/assertion code implicated by the issue. Because the crash is described as an X86 DAG combine assertion about low-bits constraints, removing unrelated generic legalization support is not evidence of a direct fix or cause. The commit could still change whether certain DAG shapes reach X86 combines, but the retrieved hunks do not show that connection.
Causal confidence: 0.14
Build risk: Reverts core SelectionDAG legalization behavior; May change whether vector intrinsics are expanded or left as nodes; Affects multiple legalization passes and intrinsic lowering; Could alter backend codegen for targets using CTTZ_ELTS

top_candidates.subject: [SelectionDAG] Optimize 32-bit udiv with 33-bit magic constants on 64-bit targets (#181288)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit extends SelectionDAG's constant unsigned-division optimization to optionally widen 32-bit scalar divisions on 64-bit targets when wide 64-bit multiply/high-multiply support is available. It introduces a widen path that computes the quotient via 64-bit zero-extension, 64x64->128 multiplication, and truncation of the high half, and updates tests to expect new x86_64 codegen for constant divisions.
Changed symbols: TargetLowering::BuildUDIV; AllowWiden; HasWideVT64MULHU; HasWideVT64UMUL_LOHI; UseWiden; MagicFactor; llvm/test/CodeGen/X86/udiv-const-optimization.ll; llvm/test/CodeGen/X86/fold-loop-of-urem.ll
Behavioral change: BuildUDIV now permits a widened optimization for 32-bit scalar unsigned division on 64-bit targets.; When widening is chosen, the divisor magic constant is materialized as i64 and the quotient is computed with MULHU/UMUL_LOHI on zero-extended operands.; The optimization path is explicitly restricted by target support for wide 64-bit multiply/high-multiply operations.

Summary: This commit changes SelectionDAG overflow expansion for signed add/sub with overflow. It keeps the existing add overflow predicate but splits subtraction into its own path, using a different signed comparison/XOR formulation for SSUBO. The visible changes are in generic SelectionDAG lowering, plus X86 vector overflow tests updated to match the new lowering shape.
Changed symbols: TargetLowering::expandSADDSUBO; SelectionDAG; TargetLowering; DAGTypeLegalizer::ExpandIntRes_SADDSUBO; vec_ssubo.ll; ssub_sat_vec.ll
Behavioral change: Separates SSUBO overflow computation from SADDO instead of sharing one predicate.; Changes subtraction overflow detection from 'result < lhs XOR rhs > 0' to 'lhs < rhs XOR result < 0'.; Adjusts vector overflow codegen expectations for signed subtraction with overflow.

Reproducer link: No direct crash/assertion text from the retrieved hunks matches 'low bits constraint must survive width adjustment' or peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc.; The patch only touches signed overflow lowering, not the specific X86 bit-test combine path named in the issue.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit extends SelectionDAG/X86 handling for absolute-value nodes to preserve poison semantics when widening or combining integer abs operations. It introduces a new ISD::ABS_MIN_POISON opcode, teaches constant folding and poison analysis about it, updates DAGBuilder to emit it for the llvm.abs intrinsic when the min-int-is-poison flag is set, and broadens X86/DAG combine and integer legalization code to treat it like ABS where appropriate.
Changed symbols: widenAbs; SelectionDAG::canCreateUndefOrPoison; SelectionDAG::getNode; SelectionDAG::FoldConstantArithmetic; SelectionDAGBuilder::visitIntrinsicCall; combineSetCC; DAGTypeLegalizer::PromoteIntegerResult; ISD::isAbsOpcode
Behavioral change: Adds a new abs-like opcode that can become poison on INT_MIN instead of always producing a defined absolute value.; Changes widening/combine logic to recognize all abs opcodes, not just ISD::ABS, so transformations remain valid for poison-preserving abs.; Adjusts constant folding and poison reasoning so ABS_MIN_POISON folds to poison on signed-min constants and is treated as potentially poison-producing in demanded-bits analysis.

Summary: This change rewrites X86 lowering for BUILD_VECTOR of i1 elements to support sub-128-bit vector masks by widening through a different scalar element type, padding with poison, and using vector-in-register extension instead of a plain ANY_EXTEND. It also updates X86 codegen tests for vector overflow lowering to expect a new VPTESTMD-based mask construction sequence on AVX512 targets.

Summary: This commit revises X86 SelectionDAG lowering for BUILD_VECTOR of i1 elements. It changes the lowering strategy to track non-constant elements with a bitmask and set, scalarizes certain boolean-mask constructions when only one non-constant element is present, and replaces some select-of-all-ones/all-zeroes patterns with selects over computed immediate masks before bitcasting and concatenating vectors.
Changed symbols: LowerBUILD_VECTORvXi1; SDValue; SDLoc; NonConstMask; NonConstElts; Undefs; TrueImm; FalseImm
Behavioral change: Tracks non-constant boolean vector elements via a bitmask instead of an index list.; Changes the special-case lowering for a single non-constant element from splat-based handling to scalarized insertion.; Computes explicit true/false immediates for select nodes rather than always using all-ones/all-zeroes constants.; For v64i1, splits the mask into 32-bit halves, selects each half independently, then bitcasts and concatenates.

top_candidates.subject: [X86][GISel] Fix carry-in for selectUAddSub. (#199261)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit changes X86 GlobalISel lowering for chained unsigned add/sub carry handling. In selectUAddSub, it replaces a compare-against-1 materialization of the carry-in byte with a NEG instruction that sets EFLAGS.CF based on whether the byte is non-zero, and updates X86 GlobalISel tests to expect NEG8r instead of CMP8ri for add/sub scalar lowering.
Changed symbols: X86InstructionSelector::selectUAddSub; BuildMI; MachineInstr; Register; createVirtualRegister; NEG8r; CMP8ri
Behavioral change: Carry-in from a chained add/sub is now converted to CF via NEG on the byte value instead of CMP byte,1.; The lowering now assumes the carry-in is a SETB-style byte value (0 or 1) and materializes flags from that byte directly.; Test expectations for GlobalISel add/sub scalar lowering were updated to match the new instruction sequence.
Assertion or trace link: low bits constraint must survive width adjustment; peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc; combineBTToBitOpFlag; X86ISelLowering.cpp
Reproducer link: Clang crashes at -O1 during X86 DAG instruction selection; backend assertion during X86 SelectionDAG combine logic

Causal explanation: The retrieved hunks only affect GlobalISel carry-in lowering for add/sub and do not touch SelectionDAG combine, bit-test lowering, or X86ISelLowering.cpp. The issue description points to a DAG-combine assertion about low-bit constraints, so this commit is not directly aligned with the reported crash path. +Global variables can be marked with ``unnamed_addr`` which indicates that
+the address is not significant, only the content. Constants marked like
+this can be merged with other constants if they have the same initializer,
+and can also be duplicated. Note that a constant with significant address
+*can* be merged with a ``unnamed_addr`` constant, the result being a
+constant whose address is significant.
+
+.. warning::
+
+    Constant duplication currently makes it unsound to compare pointers
+    if either may be ``unnamed_addr``, because each reference to the
+    global in the IR may return a different pointer, and optimization
+    passes may create additional references. Optimization passes can also
+    create pointer comparisons with the expectation that the comparison
+    will return true if the object is the same, which theoretically can
+    make any usage of ``unnamed_addr`` unsound, but in practice it is
+    unlikely that input IR that does not explicitly compare pointers
+    will be affected by this issue.

top_candidates.subject: [X86] matchBinaryPermuteShuffle - match to X86ISD::SHLD funnel shift patterns (REAPPLIED) (#200604)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit extends X86 vector-shuffle combining to recognize binary permute shuffles that can be lowered to AVX512VBMI2 funnel-shift instructions (`VSHLD`/`VSHRD`-style patterns). It adds a new matcher `matchShuffleAsVSHLD` and wires it into `matchBinaryPermuteShuffle`, enabling the lowering of certain shuffle masks into `X86ISD::VSHLD` with immediate shift amounts. The accompanying tests update expected codegen from permute/shuffle sequences to `vpshld*` instructions.
Changed symbols: matchShuffleAsVSHLD; matchBinaryPermuteShuffle; lowerShuffleAsShift; X86ISD::VSHLD; vector-shuffle-combining-avx512vbmi2.ll
Behavioral change: Adds a new shuffle-pattern recognition path for funnel-shift lowering when `AllowIntDomain` and `hasVBMI2()` are true.; Computes a shift amount from the shuffle mask and may swap operands to match the equivalent commuted pattern.; Changes codegen for selected vector shuffles from generic permutes to VBMI2 funnel-shift instructions.
Assertion or trace link: low bits constraint must survive width adjustment; peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc; combineBTToBitOpFlag; X86ISelLowering.cpp
Reproducer link: The issue is a crash/assertion during X86 DAG instruction selection, specifically around bit-test/low-bits reasoning.; This commit operates in X86 shuffle lowering and funnel-shift matching, not in the bit-test combine path named by the crash.
Pass or subsystem link: X86ISelLowering.cpp; SelectionDAG combine; vector shuffle combining
Causal explanation: The patch is clearly in X86 DAG combine/lowering and therefore is backend-adjacent, but the retrieved hunks only add shuffle-to-funnel-shift matching. There is no direct evidence that it affects the low-bits constraint assertion or the `peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc`/`combineBTToBitOpFlag` logic from the issue, so it is only a weak candidate by subsystem proximity.
Causal confidence: 0.24

top_candidates.subject: [X86] Fold XOR of VGF2P8AFFINEQB and its source (#198448)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit adds a new X86 combine that folds XOR of a `VGF2P8AFFINEQB` result with its source operand by algebraically absorbing the XOR into the affine matrix. The implementation introduces special handling for `GF2P8AFFINEQB(x, M) ^ x`, constructs a transformed matrix using an identity matrix XOR, and preserves the existing fold for XOR with a constant splat. The tests add several AVX/AVX512 cases covering source-XOR folding, nonzero immediates, alternative matrices, and multi-use non-folding behavior.
Changed symbols: combineXorWithGF2P8AFFINEQB; X86::isConstantSplat; getTargetConstantBitsFromNode; GF2P8AFFINEQB; gfni-xor-fold.ll; gfni-xor-fold-avx512.ll; gfni-operand-and-fold.ll
Behavioral change: Adds a new algebraic fold for `GF2P8AFFINEQB(x, M) ^ x` into a single `GF2P8AFFINEQB` with a transformed matrix.; Keeps the existing constant-splat XOR fold and distinguishes multi-use/variable cases to avoid incorrect folding.; Introduces new matrix-construction logic based on extracted constant bits and an identity matrix.
Assertion or trace link: low bits constraint must survive width adjustment; peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc; combineBTToBitOpFlag; X86ISelLowering.cpp
Reproducer link: The issue is a crash in X86 DAG instruction selection on a reduced C testcase.; The retrieved hunks are about GFNI XOR folding and do not mention bit-test lowering, trunc/ext peeking, or low-bits constraints.
Pass or subsystem link: X86ISelLowering.cpp; SelectionDAG combine
Causal explanation: Although this is a substantive X86 combine change in the same lowering file, it targets GFNI affine-XOR algebra rather than the bit-test/width-adjustment path implicated by the assertion. The tests confirm codegen changes for GFNI patterns only, so there is no direct evidence tying it to the reported crash.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit adds SelectionDAG legalization support for widening vector atomic stores, including a new WidenVecOp_ATOMIC_STORE helper and a coerceStoredValue routine that extracts the original-width value from a widened vector before emitting an atomic store. It also updates the vector type legalizer dispatch and adds X86 atomic store tests for several <2 x T> cases. The change is directly in SelectionDAG type legalization and atomic store lowering, which is adjacent to the reported X86 DAG combine crash area.
Changed symbols: coerceStoredValue; DAGTypeLegalizer::WidenVecOp_ATOMIC_STORE; DAGTypeLegalizer::WidenVectorOperand; LegalizeTypes.h::WidenVecOp_ATOMIC_STORE; llvm/test/CodeGen/X86/atomic-load-store.ll
Behavioral change: Adds a new legalization path for ISD::ATOMIC_STORE on widened vectors.; Computes a memory type with findMemType using the widened vector width and original store width, then coerces the widened value down to the stored width.; Preserves atomicity by emitting a single atomic store of the chosen first vector type instead of scalarizing or leaving the operation unsupported.; Uses StAlign=0 to avoid widening the access past the intended object based on alignment.

top_candidates.subject: [X86] Merge BT with a matching BTR/BTS/BTC (#193612)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This change adds X86 DAG combine support to merge a BT with a sibling bit-modifying operation into a single flag-producing BTR/BTS/BTC node, and introduces new X86ISD nodes and patterns to select those instructions. The combine explicitly peeks through truncation, zero-extension, any-extension, and AND masks that preserve the low log2(width) bits of the bit position, then reuses the original bit index when forming the merged node.
Changed symbols: peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc; combineBTToBitOpFlag; combineBT; X86btr; X86bts; X86btc; X86ISD::BTR; X86ISD::BTS
Behavioral change: Adds a new combine that fuses BT with matching BTR/BTS/BTC-style bit modifications on the same source operand.; Introduces a low-bit-preservation check for bit positions across trunc/zext/anyext and AND masks, with an assertion that the low-bit constraint survives width adjustment.; Reuses the BT bit index directly when creating the merged flag-producing node, relying on same-width i32/i64 operands.
Assertion or trace link: low bits constraint must survive width adjustment; peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc; combineBTToBitOpFlag; X86ISelLowering.cpp; SelectionDAG combine; BT
Reproducer link: Clang crashes at -O1 during X86 DAG instruction selection; assertion in backend combine logic
Pass or subsystem link: X86 target lowering; SelectionDAG combine; bit-test lowering

The new helper explicitly asserts the low-bit invariant and changes BT combine behavior, making it highly plausible as a source of the bug or a nearby regression point. The added tests also exercise masked and extended bit positions, reinforcing the connection to the reported failure mode.

top_candidates.subject: [X86] lowerShuffleWithPSHUFB - use getConstVector to create shuffle mask (#201122)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This change rewrites X86 PSHUFB shuffle-mask construction in lowerShuffleWithPSHUFB to build an integer mask vector and materialize it through getConstVector instead of assembling a vector of SDValues with explicit UNDEF/constant nodes. The functional lowering path still ends in X86ISD::PSHUFB, but the mask representation and bit-pattern materialization are changed, which can alter how SelectionDAG recognizes and combines shuffle/truncation patterns.
Changed symbols: lowerShuffleWithPSHUFB; getConstVector; X86ISD::PSHUFB
Behavioral change: Changes shuffle-mask construction from per-lane SDValue constants/UNDEFs to an integer mask vector passed through getConstVector.; Changes the final lowering shape from bitcast(PSHUFB(bitcast(V), buildvector(mask))) to bitcast(PSHUFB(bitcast(V), constvector(mask))).; Preserves the same intended shuffle semantics, but may affect DAG combine visibility and canonicalization of shuffle masks.
Assertion or trace link: X86 DAG combine; SelectionDAG; X86ISelLowering.cpp; low bits constraint must survive width adjustment; peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc; combineBTToBitOpFlag
Reproducer link: Clang crashes at -O1 during X86 DAG instruction selection; backend assertion during combine/lowering
Pass or subsystem link: X86 target lowering; SelectionDAG combine
Causal explanation: The issue is specifically about BT/bit-test lowering and low-bit-width reasoning in X86 DAG combines. This commit only touches PSHUFB shuffle-mask lowering, not BT/BTR/BTS/BTC combines or the width-adjustment assertion path named in the report. It is in a high-risk X86 lowering file, so it could influence DAG shape indirectly, but the retrieved hunks do not show a direct link to the asserted low-bits invariant.
Causal confidence: 0.18

@@ -0,0 +1,67 @@
+; Check that convert_ builtins pick the signed/unsigned opcode from the source
+; operand signedness.
+
+; RUN: llc -O0 -mtriple=spirv32-unknown-unknown %s -o - | FileCheck %s
+; RUN: %if spirv-tools %{ llc -O0 -mtriple=spirv32-unknown-unknown %s -o - -filetype=obj | spirv-val %}
+
+; CHECK-DAG: OpName %[[#StoS:]] "s_to_s"
+; CHECK-DAG: OpName %[[#StoU:]] "s_to_u"
+; CHECK-DAG: OpName %[[#UtoS:]] "u_to_s"
+; CHECK-DAG: OpName %[[#UtoU:]] "u_to_u"
+; CHECK-DAG: OpName %[[#StoF:]] "s_to_f"
+; CHECK-DAG: OpName %[[#UtoF:]] "u_to_f"
+
+; signed source -> signed dest: sign-extend.
+; CHECK: %[[#StoS]] = OpFunction
+; CHECK: OpSConvert
+define spir_func void @s_to_s(i32 noundef %x) {
+  call spir_func i64 @_Z12convert_longi(i32 noundef %x)
+  ret void
+}
+
+; signed source -> unsigned dest: sign-extend.
+; CHECK: %[[#StoU]] = OpFunction
+; CHECK: OpSConvert
+define spir_func void @s_to_u(i32 noundef %x) {
+  call spir_func i64 @_Z13convert_ulongi(i32 noundef %x)
+  ret void
+}
+
+; unsigned source -> signed dest: zero-extend.
+; CHECK: %[[#UtoS]] = OpFunction
+; CHECK: OpUConvert
+define spir_func void @u_to_s(i32 noundef %x) {
+  call spir_func i64 @_Z12convert_longj(i32 noundef %x)
+  ret void
+}
+
+; unsigned source -> unsigned dest: zero-extend.
+; CHECK: %[[#UtoU]] = OpFunction
+; CHECK: OpUConvert
+define spir_func void @u_to_u(i32 noundef %x) {
+  call spir_func i64 @_Z13convert_ulongj(i32 noundef %x)
+  ret void
+}
+
+; signed source -> float.
+; CHECK: %[[#StoF]] = OpFunction
+; CHECK: OpConvertSToF
+define spir_func void @s_to_f(i32 noundef %x) {
+  call spir_func float @_Z13convert_floati(i32 noundef %x)
+  ret void
+}
